one_line: Porwad Jain merchant-minister brothers of the late Solanki–Vaghela era, famed patrons of Luna Vasahi and civic works in Gujarat.

appearance.age_look: Vastupal appears in his late 30s, medium height and slightly sturdy; Tejpal appears in his early 30s, a little slimmer and taller, both with healthy builds from active travel and administration.
appearance.face: Both have oval faces with sharp noses and warm medium-brown complexions; Vastupal has a short well-kept beard and thoughtful, calm eyes with a gentle smile, while Tejpal is clean-shaven with livelier eyes and a more energetic, confident smile.
appearance.hair: Both keep their hair neatly pulled back under small white Marugurjara-style turbans wrapped close to the head, with a short tail at the back; Vastupal’s turban has a narrow red band, Tejpal’s has a narrow dark green band.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate late 12th–13th century western Indian merchant-official dress: both wear long-sleeved knee-length angarkha-style tunics that overlap and tie on the right, Vastupal’s in soft cream cotton with a subtle light-gold woven border at the cuffs and hem, Tejpal’s in pale leaf-green with a thin darker green border; both have slim-fit white cotton churidar-style trousers gathered at the ankles, and plain brown leather sandals; over the tunics they each wear a light woollen shawl in off-white draped over both shoulders (Vastupal’s edging is red and gold, Tejpal’s is green and gold), and a simple cloth kamarband (waist sash) – rust red for Vastupal, deep green for Tejpal – knotted slightly to the side; jewellery is modest but refined: both wear small gold stud earrings, a single thin gold chain at the neck, and a narrow gold bangle on the right wrist, with a small tilak-like sandal mark on the forehead, kept faint to respect Jain sensibilities.
appearance.signature: A detailed rolled architectural parchment tied with a red cord held in Vastupal’s left hand, and a small portable measuring staff (a straight wooden measuring rod with subtle carved markings and a brass cap at each end) held by Tejpal, symbolising their joint planning of temples, wells and civic works.

ref_desc: Two Porwad Jain brothers: Vastupal with cream angarkha, rust-red sash, off-white shawl with red-gold edge, white churidar, brown sandals, short beard, white turban with red band and rolled architectural parchment; Tejpal with pale green angarkha, green sash and shawl border, white churidar, brown sandals, clean-shaven, white turban with green band and a wooden measuring rod.
sheet_prompt: Draw an anime-style full-body model sheet of two late 13th-century western Indian Porwad Jain merchant-minister brothers standing side by side, designed to be redrawn consistently: both with warm medium-brown complexions, oval faces and sharp noses, big expressive shonen eyes, and dignified yet approachable expressions; Vastupal slightly shorter and sturdier, with a short well-kept beard, calm gentle eyes, wearing a cream long-sleeved knee-length angarkha that overlaps and ties on the right, edged with a subtle light-gold border at cuffs and hem, slim white churidar trousers gathered at the ankles, brown leather sandals, a rust-red cloth waist sash knotted slightly to the side, and an off-white shawl with a red-and-gold border draped over both shoulders; on his head a small close-wrapped white Marugurjara-style turban with a narrow red band and a short tail at the back, and modest jewellery: small gold studs, a thin gold chain, and a narrow gold bangle on the right wrist; in his left hand he holds a rolled architectural parchment tied with a red cord; beside him, Tejpal a little taller and slimmer, clean-shaven with brighter, more energetic eyes, wearing a pale leaf-green angarkha with a thin darker green border, white churidar trousers, brown sandals, a deep green waist sash, and an off-white shawl with a green-and-gold border over both shoulders, the same style of small white turban but with a narrow dark green band; he carries a straight wooden measuring rod with carved markings and brass-capped ends in his right hand; keep the clothing era-accurate and fully modest, with no fantasy armor, and emphasise the cream, white, rust red, leaf green and brown palette against a neutral background so the designs of face, hair, garments and signature tools are clear from head to toe.
